# `react/hoverIntent`

Two delays and a cancel: a panel opens after the pointer has meant it and closes after it
has left, which is what keeps a menu from flickering under a moving cursor. `useHoverDismiss` is the
other half — closing when the pointer leaves the panel itself.

## Example

```ts
import { useHoverIntent, type HoverIntent } from 'lightweight-magic-charts';

export function useMenuIntent(): HoverIntent {
  return useHoverIntent();
}
```

## Exports

- **`HOVER_CLOSE_DELAY_MS`** · value · `300`
- **`HOVER_OPEN_DELAY_MS`** · value · `140`
- **`HoverDismissOptions`** · type · `interface HoverDismissOptions { enabled: boolean; onDismiss: () => void; delayMs?: number | undefined }`
- **`HoverIntent`** · type · `interface HoverIntent { open: (run: () => void) => void; close: (run: () => void) => void; cancel: () => void }`
- **`useHoverDismiss`** · value · `(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, { enabled, onDismiss, delayMs }: HoverDismissOptions) => void`
- **`useHoverIntent`** · value · `(openDelayMs?: number, closeDelayMs?: number) => HoverIntent`
